title: Bede on Mark 1:2
body: “Being about to write his Gospel, Mark rightly puts first the testimonies of the Prophets, that he might notify to all, that what he should write was to be received without scruple of doubt, in that he shewed that these things were beforehand foretold by the Prophets.”
author: Bede, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 1:2 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Al ir a escribir su Evangelio, Marcos pone con razón primero los testimonios de los profetas, para avisar a todos que lo que iba a escribir debía recibirse sin escrúpulo de duda, pues mostraba que estas cosas habían sido anunciadas de antemano por los profetas.”

title: Bede on Mark 2:1
body: “Because the compassion of God deserts not even carnal persons, He accords to them the grace of His presence, by which even they may be made spiritual. After the desert, the Lord returns into the city.”
author: Bede, in Marc., 1, 10, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 2:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Porque la compasión de Dios no abandona ni siquiera a las personas carnales, les concede la gracia de su presencia, por la cual aun ellas pueden hacerse espirituales. Después del desierto, el Señor vuelve a la ciudad.”

title: Bede on Mark 3:1
body: “For, since He had defended the breaking of the sabbath, which they objected to His disciples, by an approved example, now they wish, by watching Him, to calumniate Himself, that they might accuse Him of a transgression, if He cured on the sabbath, of cruelty or of folly, if He refused.”
author: Bede, in Marc., 1, 14, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 3:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Porque, como había defendido el quebrantar el sábado, que objetaban a sus discípulos, con un ejemplo aprobado, ahora quieren, observándolo, calumniarlo a él mismo, para acusarlo de transgresión si curaba en sábado, o de crueldad o de necedad si se negaba.”

title: Bede on Mark 4:1
body: “For if we look into the Gospel of Matthew, it appears that this same teaching of the Lord at the sea, was delivered on the same day as the former. For after the conclusion of the first sermon, Matthew immediately subjoins, saying, "The same day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea-side.”
author: Bede, in Marc., 1, 18, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 4:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Porque si miramos el Evangelio de Mateo, parece que esta misma enseñanza del Señor junto al mar se dio el mismo día que la anterior. Pues, después de concluir el primer sermón, Mateo añade enseguida, diciendo: «Y aquel día, saliendo Jesús de casa, se sentó junto á la mar».”

title: Bede on Mark 5:1
body: “Geraza is a noted town of Arabia, across the Jordan, near mount Galaad, which the tribe of Manasseh held, not far from the lake of Tiberias, into which the swine were precipitated.”
author: Bede, in Marc., 2, 21, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 5:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Gerasa es una ciudad notable de Arabia, al otro lado del Jordán, cerca del monte Galaad, que poseía la tribu de Manasés, no lejos del lago de Tiberíades, en el cual se precipitaron los cerdos.”

title: Bede on Mark 6:1
body: “He means by His country, Nazareth, in which He was brought up. But how great the blindness of the Nazarenes!”
author: Bede, in Marc., 2, 23, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 6:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Por su tierra entiende Nazaret, donde fue criado. ¡Pero qué grande es la ceguera de los nazarenos!”

title: Bede on Mark 7:1
body: “The people of the land of Gennesareth, who seemed to be unlearned men, not only come themselves, but also bring their sick to the Lord, that they may but succeed in touching the hem of His garment. But the Pharisees and Scribes, who ought to have been the teachers of the people, run together to the Lord, not to seek for healing, but to move captious questions.”
author: Bede, in Marc., 2, 29, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 7:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “La gente de la tierra de Genesaret, que parecían hombres sin letras, no solo vienen ellos, sino que también traen a sus enfermos al Señor, con tal de lograr tocar el borde de su manto. Pero los fariseos y los escribas, que debían haber sido los maestros del pueblo, corren juntos al Señor, no para buscar sanidad, sino para mover preguntas capciosas.”

title: Bede on Mark 8:1
body: “The typical difference between this feeding and the other of the five loaves and two fishes, is, that there the letter of the Old Testament, full of spiritual grace, is signified, but here the truth and grace of the New Testament, which is to be ministered to all the faithful, is pointed out.”
author: Bede, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 8:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “La diferencia figurada entre esta comida y la otra de los cinco panes y dos peces es que allí se significa la letra del Antiguo Testamento, llena de gracia espiritual, y aquí se señala la verdad y la gracia del Nuevo Testamento, que ha de ministrarse a todos los fieles.”

title: Bede on Mark 9:1
body: “Our Saviour then when transfigured did not lose the substance of real flesh, but shewed forth the glory of His own or of our future resurrection; for such as He then appeared to the Apostles, He will after the judgment appear to all His elect.”
author: Bede, 3, 37, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 9:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Nuestro Salvador, al transfigurarse, no perdió la sustancia de la carne verdadera, sino que mostró la gloria de su propia resurrección o de la nuestra futura; porque tal como entonces apareció a los apóstoles, después del juicio aparecerá a todos sus elegidos.”

title: Bede on Mark 10:1
body: “Up to this time, Mark hath related what Our Lord said and did in Galilee; here he begins to relate what He did, taught, or suffered in Judaea, and first indeed across the Jordan on the east; and this is what is said in these words: "And He arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judaea, by the farther side of Jordan"; then also on this side Jordan, when He came to Jericho, Bethany, and Jerusalem.”
author: Bede, In Marcum, 3, 40, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 10:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Hasta aquí Marcos ha contado lo que nuestro Señor dijo e hizo en Galilea; aquí empieza a contar lo que hizo, enseñó o padeció en Judea, y primero, en efecto, al otro lado del Jordán, al oriente; y esto es lo que se dice en estas palabras: «Y partiéndose de allí, vino á los términos de Judea y tras el Jordán»; luego también de este lado del Jordán, cuando vino a Jericó, Betania y Jerusalén.”

title: John Chrysostom on Mark 11:1
body: “Now that the Lord had given sufficient proof of His virtue, and the cross was at hand, even at the door, He did those things which were about to excite them against Him with a greater openness; therefore although He had so often gone up to Jerusalem, He never however had done so in such a conspicuous manner as now.”
author: John Chrysostom, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 11:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Ahora que el Señor había dado prueba suficiente de su virtud, y la cruz estaba cerca, ya a la puerta, hizo con mayor claridad aquellas cosas que iban a excitarlos contra él; por eso, aunque tantas veces había subido a Jerusalén, nunca lo había hecho de una manera tan visible como ahora.”

title: Bede on Mark 12:1
body: “Or else, the hedge is the wall of the city, the winefat is the altar, or those winefats, by which three psalms receive their name.”
author: Bede, in Marc., 3, 42, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 12:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “O bien, el seto es el muro de la ciudad, el lagar es el altar, o aquellos lagares por los cuales tres salmos reciben su nombre.”

title: Bede on Mark 13:1
body: “Because after the founding of the Church of Christ, Judaea was to be punished for her treachery, the Lord fitly, after praising the devotedness of the Church in the person of the poor widow, goes out of the temple, and foretold its coming ruin, and the contempt in which the buildings now so wonderful were soon to be held.”
author: Bede, in Marc., iv, 42, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 13:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Porque, después de fundada la Iglesia de Cristo, Judea había de ser castigada por su traición, el Señor, con razón, después de alabar la devoción de la Iglesia en la persona de la viuda pobre, sale del templo y anunció su ruina venidera, y el desprecio en que pronto se tendrían los edificios ahora tan admirables.”

title: Bede on Mark 14:1
body: “Pascha, which in Hebrew is, phase, is not called from Passion, as many think, but from passing over, because the destroyer, seeing the blood on the doors of the Israelites, passed by them, and did not smite them; or the Lord Himself, bringing aid unto His people, walked above them.”
author: Bede, Marc., iv, 43, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 14:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Pascua, que en hebreo es phase, no se llama así por la Pasión, como muchos piensan, sino por el pasar de largo, porque el destructor, al ver la sangre en las puertas de los israelitas, pasó de largo y no los hirió; o el Señor mismo, trayendo auxilio a su pueblo, caminó por encima de ellos.”

title: Bede on Mark 15:1
body: “The Jews had a custom of delivering him whom they had condemned to death, bound to the judge.”
author: Bede, in Marc., 4, 44, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 15:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Los judíos tenían la costumbre de entregar atado al juez a aquel a quien habían condenado a muerte.”

title: Gregory on Mark 16:1
body: “But if we believe on Him who is dead, and are filled with the sweet smell of virtue, and seek the Lord with the fame of good works, we come to His sepulchre with spices.”
author: Gregory, Hom. in. Evan., 21, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Mark 16:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)
bodyEs: “Pero si creemos en el que está muerto, y estamos llenos del olor suave de la virtud, y buscamos al Señor con la fama de las buenas obras, llegamos a su sepulcro con especias.”
